intuition: An evolutionary search improves candidates by repeatedly applying an evaluator. The evaluator determines what improvement means.
learningGoal: Explore AlphaEvolve-style algorithm search: generate candidates, evaluate correctness and fitness, and retain measurable improvements.
exerciseNote: CPU-only Python: run the miniature numerical optimizer. It illustrates mutation and selection, not the full AlphaEvolve system.

quiz.question: An AI optimization agent generates two implementations of a scheduling algorithm. Candidate A: 20% faster than the baseline, but violates the required latency SLO for some workloads. Candidate B: 12% faster than the baseline and satisfies all required constraints in the evaluation. Which candidate is preferable for further validation?
quiz.explanation: Candidate B satisfies the evaluated constraints. It still needs further validation; passing this evaluation does not establish performance on every workload.
choices: Candidate A, because it is the fastest.
Candidate B, because it improves performance while satisfying the evaluated constraints.
Whichever candidate was generated most recently.
Both should immediately be deployed without further testing.
